research_question: Can a hardware-aware multi-objective optimizer identify near-Pareto-optimal LLM inference configurations using substantially fewer measurements than exhaustive search?

comparison.note: exhaustive wall-clock grid; one measurement per configuration
mean ± 95% t-interval over 5 seeds at budget 4
mean ± 95% t-interval over 5 seeds at budget 4
mean ± 95% t-interval over 5 seeds at budget 4

note: Grid is measured once on the wall clock. Random, InferLite, and the heuristic replay those records at each seed×budget; they do not invent tokens/s or latency. InferLite still chooses sequentially: the surrogate only sees points it has already picked. On this design InferLite uses the ridge model only after three measured points, so budget 2 is a diverse/heuristic seed, not surrogate search.
